stories.title: Binance to resume withdrawals after covering bulk of stolen $6.3bn
summary: Binance, the worlds biggest cryptocurrency exchange, said it would resume withdrawals on Sunday after covering 95 per cent of the $6.3 billion in tokens stolen from its platform in the world’s largest digital heist, which the FBI has tied to North Korea.
Binance said on Sunday it had covered $6bn of stolen cryptocurrencies by using company money to buy replacement tokens.
Analysts had blamed North Korea and said the Binance theft could be the largest financial heist of all time.

stories.title: Official records ‘stolen’ from Bannu TMA office
summary: BANNU: The theft of official records from the Tehsil Municipal Administration (TMA), Bannu, has come to light, with important registers and files reportedly missing from the Tehsil Officer Regulation (TOR) branch.
In a complaint submitted to the city police station, the administration said that the drawers and cupboards of the branch were found unlocked when the office reopened last Monday.
TMA Bannu Tehsil Municipal Officer Fakhrul Islam requested the police to register a first information report and launch an investigation to recover the missing official records.

stories.title: 12 dilapidated classrooms of Charsadda school sealed
summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Secretary Dr Mohammad Fakhre Alam Irfan had taken notice of the dilapidated condition of the school building after reports and photographs highlighting the plight of students went viral on social media.
DEO Fazal Wahid visited the school accompanied by deputy DEO Zubair Khalil, DEO planning and development Shiraz Hussain and other officials.
The school principal, Mohammad Ayaz Khan, briefed the officials on the deteriorating condition of the building, difficulties faced by students and the impact on academic activities.

stories.title: Woman dies by suicide after ‘strangling’ minor daughter in Bajaur
summary: BAJAUR: A woman allegedly committed suicide after ‘strangling’ her minor daughter to death in War Mamond tehsil of Bajaur district on Saturday, police and residents said.
A police official told Dawn that a team rushed to the spot after receiving information about the incident and the bodies were taken to the District Headquarters Hospital in Khar for postmortem.
Mansoor Khan, a spokesperson for the district police, told reporters that an investigation had been launched to ascertain the causes behind the incident.

stories.title: Mob torches trailer after pregnant woman’s death in Karachi's Liaquatabad
summary: KARACHI: Enraged people set a trailer on fire after it ran over and killed a pregnant woman and injured her husband in a road accident in Liaquatabad, police said on Saturday.

A traffic police officer said that the couple was travelling on a motorbike when the trailer hit them as they descended from the Liaquatabad flyover and approached the Sindh Government Hospital Liaquatabad on S M Taufiq Road.
SITE-Superhighway Industrial Area SHO Mohammad Nawaz said the driver fled the scene, while police had seized the heavy vehicle.

stories.title: Disciplinary proceedings against Karachi's Valika hospital employees over HIV outbreak slow, regrets ombudsman
summary: The ombudsman said that his office had finalised the criminal proceedings against these employees of the hospital [run under the Sindh Employees Social Security Institution], “but it is unfortunate to see the disciplinary proceeding against them at a slow pace”.

Mr Rajput said that there were around 8,000 complaints that used to be handled by this office annually until he took the charge of the ombudsman’s office. “Now the average annual number is around 25,000 i.e. three times higher,” he pointed out.
Explaining the initiatives, the ombudsman said his office engaged 10 brand ambassadors, from each of Sindh’s universities, for the projection of the office’s working through digital means.

stories.title: Two dead as car, bike fall into canal after collision in Multan
summary: LAHORE: A man and a woman were killed while another woman and a two-year-old girl were injured when a car collided with a motorcycle and both vehicles fell into a canal near Muhammad Nawaz Sharif University of Agriculture, Multan on Saturday.
Four people, including two women, were riding the motorcycle when it collided with the car.
Separately, Multan Rescue 1122 responded to 469 emergencies across the district during the last 24 hours, rescuing 472 people, according to its daily report issued on Saturday.

stories.title: Kasur woman suffers burns in acid attack by brother-in-law
summary: KASUR: A woman was seriously injured after her brother-in-law allegedly threw acid on her in the Purani Mandi Area in the limits of Pattoki City police station on Saturday.
According to the police, Shahbaz allegedly threw acid on his sister-in-law, leaving her in a seriously injured condition with burns on her face and other parts of the body.
ELECTROCUTION: A 12-year-old boy was electrocuted after live wires fell on him at Ratti Pindi village in the limits of Kot Radha Kishan police station.

stories.title: World Bank okays $150m plan to boost property tax collection in Karachi
summary: ISLAMABAD: The World Bank has approved a $150 million programme to help the Sindh government improve urban property tax collection and strengthen municipal service delivery in 25 towns of Karachi.
The Sindh Property Revenues Enhancement Programme (Sindh PREP) approved by the World Bank board of executive directors, will benefit Karachi’s 25 local councils.

This programme will help Sindh strengthen fiscal sustainability enabling cities to plan, invest, and deliver services from their own resources effectively,” said Davison Muchadenyika, senior urban development specialist at the World Bank.

stories.title: In Spectrum: Gymkhana: colonial origins and politics of selective outrage
summary: Partition in 1947 dismantled the political and social order that had sustained colonial institutions, yet Lahore Gymkhana survived and gradually became part of the civilian life of ‘independent’ Pakistan.
This combination of historical continuity, social adaptation and member-based governance makes Lahore Gymkhana a distinctive institution in Pakistan’s civic landscape.

These questions do not absolve Lahore Gymkhana of accountability; they expose the inconsistency of targeting a civilian institution while comparable arrangements elsewhere may escape equivalent examination.

stories.title: Federal prison law draft sent to interior ministry for approval
summary: Officials familiar with the matter told Dawn that the Act was being drafted to provide for the establishment, management, safety and security of prisons, the care and custody of prisoners, their reformation and rehabilitation, and related matters.

According to the proposed draft, the objectives of the Federal Prison System include contributing to the maintenance and protection of a just, peaceful and safe society by enforcing sentences awarded by courts, the Act and its regulations in the prescribed manner.
It shall also establish an Oversight Committee for prisoners’ welfare, philanthropic initiatives, rehabilitation programmes, monitoring of prison administration or any other related purpose.

stories.title: Double murder suspects killed in CCD shootout in Attock
summary: A police spokesperson claimed that the suspects were killed by their own accomplices during an exchange of fire near Bota village on Bhattiyot Road.

Police said the suspects were wanted in connection with the abduction and murder of two persons in Fatehjang, including 11-year-old Saim Raza, who was reportedly taken from Vehari, and an unidentified mentally disabled man abducted from the Rawat area along G.T.
The investigation by Fatehjang police reportedly exposed the alleged double murder and identified the complainants as the main suspects.

stories.title: PTI seeks extension in Islamabad LG polls nomination deadline
summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) Islamabad chapter has demanded that the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) should extend the deadline for submission of nomination papers for the upcoming local government elections in the capital by at least 10 days.

PTI Islamabad president and core committee member Amir Mughal, while talking to Dawn, alleged that candidates were unable to obtain nomination papers on Friday despite the schedule issued by the ECP for the elections in 125 union councils.
He said Islamabad had traditionally been a stronghold of PTI and expressed confidence that the party would perform strongly in the local elections.

stories.title: US hears Pakistan’s concerns over terrorism from Afghanistan, would play ‘productive role’ if there is one: Rubio
summary: Mentioning that the US did not “necessarily [have] the closest relationship” with the Afghan Taliban, Rubio added: “We’ve heard the concerns that Pakistan has raised and we’ve seen some of those attacks that they point to.

For their part, the Afghan Taliban have avoided taking a categorical position on the TTP and other groups, while rejecting Islamabad’s allegations that Afghanistan is being used as a base for attacks against Pakistan.

On Saturday, Pakistan’s information ministry rebuked the Afghan Taliban’s stance on the ongoing conflict between the two countries, assailing its “persistent refusal to address terrorism” emanating from Afghanistan’s soil.

stories.title: Consumer firms defy economic headwinds
summary: Local and multinational companies post robust sales growth this year Net profit after tax rose 3.1pc to Rs14.526bn from Rs14.1bn a year earlier, despite higher tax expenses.
Unilever Pakistan Unilever Pakistan Foods’ sales rose to Rs37.6bn in the first nine months of 2026 from Rs30bn a year earlier, while profit after tax increased to Rs6.326bn from Rs4.6bn.
However, renewed inflation, higher global commodity and energy prices, and Middle East tensions continued to constrain consumer spending, the company added.

stories.title: India’s water blackmail
summary: India’s primary target in this strategic campaign is the Chenab river, which it is systematically converting into a long-term instrument of leverage to dictate Pakistan’s foreign policy, weaken its stance on Kashmir, and dominate bilateral relations.
Therefore, Islamabad must view India’s decision to place the IWT in abeyance as another dimension of New Delhi’s long-standing and coordinated policy of economic strangulation of Pakistan.
Pakistan must declare a national water emergency, educate vulnerable communities in 11 districts of central Punjab that depend on the Chenab, expedite dam construction, and modernise irrigation.

stories.title: Retired officials call for respecting people’s wishes
summary: In a statement shared with Dawn on Saturday, the Roedad Khan Club, often described as Islamabad’s ‘retired establishment’ because it comprises retired but influential officials, said constitutional rule must be restored in practice rather than maintained as a facade.
Seek equal treatment of provinces, warn against constitutional changes imposed against public will “Constitutional rule needs to be restored as a reality, and not as a facade.

The club also rejected what it described as hybrid governance, arguing that a system “in which elected civilian institutions operate alongside an unelected centre of power deepens political resentment and undermines constitutional rule”.

stories.title: Uncertain local governments
summary: Currently, the ECP is fighting a four-way battle — with the provincial governments of Punjab and KP, the federal government, and the cantonment boards — for LG elections in the two provinces, Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT), and the cantonment boards.
For more than five years, the ECP and the federal government have been haggling over legal points and the possible date of the next election.
The cantonment boards’ election has an additional prerequisite: the ECP should receive the federal government’s request before holding the election.

stories.title: ECP begins registration of voters in Punjab's Kasur, Sindh's Qamber-Shahdadkot
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Saturday announced a pilot project to reduce the gender gap in voter registration in Kasur district of Punjab and Qamber-Shahdadkot district of Sindh.
According to the ECP, data collection for the initiative will be carried out in November 2026, while voter registration activities will continue from December 2026 to February 2027.
Through the campaign, the ECP aims to facilitate the registration of 115,689 women in Kasur and 59,156 in Qamber-Shah­dadkot.

stories.title: Islamabad High Court bars FIR mention in character certificates after acquittal
summary: It held that following an acquittal, there was no legal justification for portraying an individual as an accused or criminal through a police-issued character certificate.

Rules such mention violates constitutional rights, including dignity and freedom of movement Allowing the petition, the court ordered the removal of a reference to an FIR registered at Shalimar Police Station from the petitioner’s character certificate.

The court held that including an FIR in a character certificate despite an individual’s acquittal violated Articles 4, 9, 14 and 15 of the Constitution, which protect citizens’ rights, liberty, dignity and freedom of movement.

stories.title: Cost of provinces
summary: The figures expose a major weakness in the argument for creating more provinces: political and administrative restructuring is often presented as an inexpensive way to make government more responsive.

Political parties’ record of repeatedly suspending, delaying or weakening elected LGs suggests that the problem is less the size of provinces than the reluctance of political leadership to devolve power and resources.
Political parties demanding new provinces must explain how they intend to pay for them and what improvements citizens can expect.

stories.title: US to deport 150 Afghan immigrants back to Kabul
summary: WASHINGTON: President Don­­ald Trump’s administration plans to deport more than 150 Afghan immigrants back to Afghanistan via Pakistan, US media reported, a move advocacy groups say could endanger their lives.

More than 150 Afghan immigrants are expected to be deported in the latest push, The New York Times reported on Friday, citing three unnamed US officials, and the first flight could leave as soon as Monday.
While the US cannot arrange deportations directly to Afgha­n­istan, the officials told the Times that Pakistan will oversee their expulsion to Afghanistan.

stories.title: LPG price twice the official rate in open market
summary: The oil and gas regulator said that the LPG producer price was linked with Saudi Aramco-CP and the US dollar exchange rate.

It added that compared to the previous month, Saudi Aramco-CP had increased by 6.47 per cent, while the average dollar exchange rate had slightly decreased by 0.12pc, resulting in an increase in the LPG consumer price by Rs14.73 per kg.
Pakistan LPG Marketers Association Cha­irman Ali Haider warned that they will observe a strike from Nov 16 if the government implemented the policy.

stories.title: MotoGP confident Qatar race can go ahead
summary: MotoGP is set to go ahead with the Qatar Grand Prix even as a group of riders demand more assurances for travelling to the region, with organisers arguing that a "zero-risk environment" is unrealistic.
"MotoGP has provided teams and riders with every assurance available from the State of Qatar, the circuit ... and our own ongoing risk assessment processes," a MotoGP spokesperson said.

Carlos Ezpeleta, deputy CEO ⁠of MotoGP, visited Qatar on Thursday, where the circuit's president, Abdulrahman Al-Mannai, said they were ready to welcome the riders, teams and fans for the 20th round of the season.

stories.title: Valkyries defeat Dream to capture first WNBA crown
summary: Gabby Williams scored 30 points and the Golden State Valkyries captured their first Women's NBA title on Saturday, defeating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in a winner-take-all championship showdown.
Williams scored a WNBA Finals one-half record 28 points in the second half as the second-year expansion Valkyries won the series four games to three, the longest title matchup in league history.

I wouldn't change a thing." Despite only two points in the first half, Williams seized command in the second with the game on the line and lifted Golden State ahead to stay in the dying minutes to earn the WNBA Finals Most Valuable Player award.

stories.title: Indian authorities tighten security ahead of big opposition march in Delhi
summary: Opposition parties, student organisations and the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party have held near-daily demonstrations since last month demanding that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar step down over the voter list revision that critics say favour the BJP.
The opposition parties have announced they will hold a nearly 1.5 km (1 mile) march on Sunday from Central Delhi to the Ramlila Maidan, a ground that is the designated site for their protest rally.

Visuals from news agency ANI showed riot control vehicles and dozens of security personnel armed with batons and shields outside the rally venue, where announcements were being made urging people to ensure smooth traffic movement and cooperate with police officials.

stories.title: SMOKERS’ CORNER: THE MYTH OF PTI’S POPULARITY
summary: In the aftermath of Khan’s arrest in 2023, PTI’s media apparatus cleverly converted the general public anger over rising inflation and political instability (which Khan’s regime left behind), into an unquestioning loyalty to the imprisoned Khan.
The illusion of overwhelming popularity unravels when passive sympathisers who express support on social media or through voting, decline to transform into active political actors on the streets.

The loss of PTI’s last institutional foothold in KP demonstrates that, while manufactured popularity and grievance-based narratives can maintain an electoral pull, they remain inherently fragile when confronted with state power, and the reality of growing public apathy.

stories.title: Sikh community’s issues to be addressed on priority: Kundi
summary: The governor was addressing a gathering at Governor House to mark the 557th birth anniversary of Baba Guru Nanak.
He also expressed the commitment to completing long-pending legislation concerning minority rights at the earliest.
On the occasion, Mr Kundi cut a cake to celebrate the 557th birth anniversary of Baba Guru Nanak.

stories.title: Zulfi Bukhari’s agricultural land in Attock put up for auction
summary: ATTOCK: Another 377 kanals agricultural land belonging to PTI leader and former federal minister Syed Zulfiqar Abbas Bukhari has been put up for public auction in Jand town of Attock on Nov 11.
The auction notice comes after 771 kanals and nine marlas and another 25 kanals and seven marlas of his agricultural land had previously been auctioned by NAB.
Zulfi Bukhari, in his post on social media platform X, said nearly 800 kanals of his agricultural land had already been auctioned and that his properties in Islamabad and Attock had been sealed.

stories.title: Dengue tally reaches 83 in Pindi with four fresh cases reported
summary: RAWALPINDI: As many as four more patients went down with the mosquito-borne disease dengue in the last two days and took the tally to 83 in the current season. “A total of four patients’ reports confirmed suffering from dengue virus in the last two days.
Seven patients were admitted in the Holy Family Hospital’s dengue ward,” said Dr Jawad, District Health Officer Preventive.

During the meeting, a detailed review was conducted regarding the overall performance of the anti-dengue campaign, the status of patients, indoor and outdoor surveillance, the detection of larvae, activities at identified hotspots and the performance of field teams.

stories.title: Repair of Bostan Road awaits approval as Pindi roads rehabilitation begins
summary: RAWALPINDI: While the Punjab Highway Department has started work on the rehabilitation of 18 roads in the garrison city at a cost of Rs6.5 billion, the reconstruction of Ch.
Bostan Khan Road, under the Rawalpindi Municipal Corporation (RMC) and District Council, to the Punjab Highway Department.
During the meeting, the DC was briefed on the status of development projects, including allocated funds, tenders and the progress of ongoing construction work.

stories.title: PIA resumes direct flights to China
summary: BEIJING: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) has resumed its flight operations between Pakistan and China with the first flight operating on Oct 30, reconnecting Islamabad and Beijing through direct air services.
In a major step towards expanding its network across China, PIA has strengthened its cooperation with three leading Chinese airlines — Air China, Shenzhen Airlines and Hainan Airlines.
Through its partnership with Air China, passengers will benefit from onward connections to various domestic destinations through Beijing, a major aviation hub.

stories.title: Kids’ social media access: FCC to hear petition on 6th
summary: LAHORE: The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) is set to hear a public interest petition seeking measures to restrict access to social media platforms by children below 16 years of age.

The petition asks the FCC to direct the federal government to amend Peca 2016 to restrict social media access for under-16s with an age-verification mechanism, and order to the Pemra to strictly enforce content standards during child-viewing hours.
It also seeks a direction to the government for coordination with social media platforms on parental controls and action on out-of-school children and dropout rates.

stories.title: ‘Medicine pricing needs serious attention’
summary: KARACHI: More than 86,000 medicines produced by pharmaceutical companies have been registered under the Track and Trace System, allowing consumers to scan products by mobile phone to check their authenticity and find out their prices, Federal Health Minister Mustafa Kamal said.
The pharmaceutical industries seek an increase in medicine prices, but the matter is under consideration by the federal cabinet.

The issue has two dimensions as an increase in medicine prices will create additional financial difficulties for ordinary citizens, while keeping prices unchanged could lead to shortages of medicines for serious illnesses.

stories.title: Interim bail granted to PTI activists in 35 pleas against detention under MPO
summary: A PHC bench comprising Justice Sahibzada Asadullah and Justice Inamullah Khan granted interim relief in around 35 petitions filed by Akbar Shah and dozens of other detainees, mostly held at Mardan Central Prison.

In their absence, the bench said, it had examined the material available on record to determine whether the petitioners qualified for interim relief, without making any final determination on their claims.
The bench also referred to three earlier petitions in which other detainees had been granted similar interim relief against furnishing surety bonds of Rs100,000 each.

stories.title: Nuclear science boosts Pakistan’s ability to track groundwater
summary: This advancement has considerably strengthened the connection between scientific research and water governance, allowing for more precise and systematic observation of groundwater dynamics across diverse hydrogeological settings, the IAEA report said.
Through its participation in the programme, Pakistan has significantly strengthened its laboratory capacity for isotope hydrology.

Policymakers are increasingly rel­ying on isotope hydrology data to inf­orm regulatory frameworks, resource allocation and long-term planning, reflecting a significant shift from reactive to preventive and science-informed groundwater management.
